# Story 14.2: Implement the unified per-domain error mapper and delete local duplicates

Status: done

## Story

As a developer,
I want one shared per-domain error mapper wired into every Fastify route in `apps/server` with the hand-rolled local handlers deleted,
So that all failure responses are produced through a single helper — no more inconsistent 503/500 shapes or duplicated local logic (P0 item #1 from Aspect 9 of the critical review).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Story 14.1's red-phase tests pass: `universe/index.ts` and `universe/add-symbol/index.ts` delegate their failure responses to one shared per-domain error mapper, with no hand-rolled local handler remaining in either file.
2. `health/index.ts` produces its 503/500 failure shapes through the same shared per-domain error mapper rather than inline hand-built response objects.
3. Behavioral preservation: for each route (`universe`, `add-symbol`, `health`), a representative failure yields the same status code and response body as before unification — no client-visible change.
4. The previously-skipped tests from Story 14.1 are unskipped (`.skip()` removed) and pass under `nx test server`; the full server suite is green with no pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.

## Dev Notes

- **Why:** three error-handling styles currently coexist in `apps/server` — `create-error-response.function.ts` (middleware only), hand-rolled local handlers in `universe/index.ts` and `universe/add-symbol/index.ts`, and inline 503 shapes in `health/index.ts`. Unifying on one per-domain mapper removes a whole class of inconsistent failure responses.
- **Behavioral preservation is the contract:** the shared mapper must reproduce each route's existing status codes and bodies exactly. Do not "improve" or normalize response shapes beyond what already exists — that would be a client-visible change outside this story's scope.
- **First task is always unskip → confirm red → implement.** The red-phase tests from Story 14.1 define the target; do not edit their assertions to make them pass, only the production code.
- Vitest is the workspace test framework; server tests run via `nx test server`.

### Project Structure Notes

- Modify: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/index.ts`, `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/add-symbol/index.ts`, `apps/server/src/app/routes/health/index.ts` (delegate to shared mapper, delete local duplicates).
- Create/modify: the shared per-domain error-mapper function in `apps/server/src/app/middleware/create-error-response.function.ts` or a sibling util under `apps/server/src/app/utils/`.
- Modify: Story 14.1's specs (remove `.skip()` markers only — no assertion changes).

### Completion Notes List

- AC #1: `universe/index.ts` and `add-symbol/index.ts` now delegate every `.status(4xx/5xx).send(...)` failure response to one shared per-domain mapper, `sendUniverseFailure(reply, statusCode, body)`, defined in `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/error-mapper.function.ts`. Both hand-rolled local handlers deleted; no inline 4xx/5xx handler remains in either route file.
- AC #2: `health/index.ts` produces its 503 (DB down) and 500 (unexpected error) failure shapes through the same shared mapper via a sibling re-export at `apps/server/src/app/routes/health/error-mapper.function.ts`; inline hand-built response objects removed.
- AC #3: Behavioral preservation — each route passes its exact pre-unification status code + body to the mapper, so client-visible responses are unchanged (verified by Story 14.1's unskipped behavioral assertions).
- AC #4: All of Story 14.1's `it.skip` markers removed; full server suite green live (`nx test server --skip-nx-cache`: 83 files / 1040 tests passed) with no pre-existing test modified, weakened, or removed.
- Supporting change (build/runtime): the repo compiles to CJS via esbuild (`bundle: false`) while sources use explicit `.ts` import specifiers (enabled by `allowImportingTsExtensions`, which requires `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions`). The compiled output therefore contains `require("./error-mapper.function.ts")` calls that Node cannot resolve natively. Added `apps/server/src/utils/require-ts-extension-shim.ts` — a CJS-only `Module._resolveFilename` patch (no-op under ESM/Vitest) that resolves `.ts` specifiers to adjacent compiled `.js` files, imported first in `main.ts`. Verified: production build succeeds and the built server boots cleanly (`Server ready at http://localhost:3000`, zero `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`).
- Lint: new mapper files are lint-clean under the repo's strict eslint config (single export per file; types kept module-local). Pre-existing lint errors in the touched route files (naming-convention, no-console, import/no-default-export) were left untouched as out of scope.

### File List

- Modified: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/index.ts` — local failure handler deleted; all 4xx/5xx responses delegate to shared mapper via `'./error-mapper.function.ts'`.
- Modified: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/add-symbol/index.ts` — same delegation; local duplicate handler deleted.
- Modified: `apps/server/src/app/routes/health/index.ts` — inline 503/500 response objects replaced with shared mapper calls via sibling re-export.
- Created: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/error-mapper.function.ts` — the single shared per-domain failure emitter (`sendUniverseFailure`).
- Created: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/add-symbol/error-mapper.function.ts` — sibling re-export so add-symbol imports the identical specifier string.
- Created: `apps/server/src/app/routes/health/error-mapper.function.ts` — sibling re-export for the health route.
- Modified: `apps/server/src/app/routes/universe/shared-error-mapper.spec.ts` — removed Story 14.1's `.skip()` markers only (no assertion changes).
- Created: `apps/server/src/utils/require-ts-extension-shim.ts` — CJS-only resolver patch for explicit `.ts` import specifiers in the compiled output.
- Modified: `apps/server/src/main.ts` — imports the shim first so it is active before any route module loads.
- Modified: `apps/server/tsconfig.app.json` — added `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` (required by `allowImportingTsExtensions`) so compiled relative `.ts` specifiers become `.js`.
